title: No good effort is ever lost

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचपार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते । नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्िचद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥
verses.tr: Krishna says: O Partha, there is no destruction for him either here or hereafter. No one who does good ever comes to a bad end, my dear.
verses.angle: Partha: the son of the earth
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna asked what happens to the person who falls short in yoga. Listen to Krishna's direct answer.

body.text: Krishna says: O Partha, there is no destruction for him either here or hereafter. No one who does good ever comes to a bad end, my dear. Krishna addresses Arjuna as Partha, son of Pritha, and then makes a promise. The one who does good practice, kalyanakrit, will never reach a bad end, durgatim. Krishna explains where that person goes after falling from yoga, to the worlds of good deeds, before being born again in a pure and prosperous home.

verses.sa: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः । शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥
verses.tr: The one who falls from yoga reaches the worlds earned by good deeds, dwells there for many long years, and is then born again in the house of the pure and prosperous.
verses.angle: yoga-bhrastah: the fallen yogi is not lost
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna speaks of a soul who tries the path of yoga but fails. Listen to the place this person returns to.

body.text: The one who falls from yoga reaches the worlds earned by good deeds, dwells there for many long years, and is then born again in the house of the pure and prosperous. The word yoga-bhrastah means one fallen from yoga. Instead of ruin, this person is born into a pure and prosperous house, carrying the memory of the path. Krishna adds that such a birth among wise yogis is very rare.

verses.sa: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् । एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥
verses.tr: Or he is born into the family of wise yogis. Such a birth is very rare in this world.
verses.angle: Yoginam: a family shaped by wisdom
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the fate of the yogi who slips. Now listen for a different possibility, one that offers a rare advantage for the one who fell.

body.text: Or he is born into the family of wise yogis. Such a birth is very rare in this world. Listen for the word yoginam, of the yogis. Instead of being born into a wealthy or pure house, the one who fell returns straight into a family shaped by wisdom and discipline, where the path can continue. Sanjaya now says that in that family he regains his old understanding and strives again toward success.

verses.sa: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् । यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥
verses.tr: O son of Kuru, there he effortlessly regains the spiritual understanding from his previous life. Then he strives again, with greater force, toward complete success.
verses.angle: The yogi regains past discernment effortlessly
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has just asked if a failed yogi is lost forever. Krishna answers by describing what happens in the next life. Listen for the two stages of recovery.

body.text: O son of Kuru, there he effortlessly regains the spiritual understanding from his previous life. Then he strives again, with greater force, toward complete success. Krishna says the yogi regains the buddhisanyoga, the spiritual understanding from his former body, effortlessly. Then he strives again with greater force toward complete success. Even against his will, he is drawn onward by that earlier practice.

verses.sa: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
verses.tr: Even against his will, he is drawn onward by that earlier practice. Even the seeker of yoga goes beyond the sound of ritual words.
verses.angle: Avashah api: even against his will
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Carrying on, Krishna tells Arjuna that the pull of past practice is so strong that a person is drawn back even when they are not in control. Listen for the word that marks this involuntary pull.

body.text: Even against his will, he is drawn onward by that earlier practice. Even the seeker of yoga goes beyond the sound of ritual words. The word avashah api means even against his will. Krishna says that past practice is so strong that it pulls a person forward even when they are not in control. Krishna then explains that this very practice also carries a seeker past the mere sound of ritual words.

verses.sa: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः । अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
verses.tr: But the yogi who keeps striving with effort, whose impurities have been cleared, and who has been perfected through many births, reaches the highest goal.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers the fear that effort can be lost. Listen to how the yogi moves from one birth to the next.

body.text: But the yogi who keeps striving with effort, whose impurities have been cleared, and who has been perfected through many births, reaches the highest goal. The word yatamanah, striving, shows that the yogi is not resting on past skill. The effort is present, continuous, and active right now. Krishna then places the yogi above all other paths of spiritual life.

verses.sa: तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः । कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥
verses.tr: The yogi is greater than ascetics, greater than scholars, and greater than workers. Therefore, Arjuna, become a yogi.
verses.angle: The direct command to become a yogi
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown how a yogi's practice survives failure. Now he ranks the yogi above all other paths and gives a direct command.

body.text: The yogi is greater than ascetics, greater than scholars, and greater than workers. Therefore, Arjuna, become a yogi. Listen to the rhythm of the word yogi. It is named three times, each time placed higher than the last, and the verse ends with a direct order to Arjuna to become one. Krishna now names the one who worships him with trust and complete absorption.

verses.sa: योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना । श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥
verses.tr: Among all yogis, the one who worships me with trust, with the inner self absorbed in me, is considered the most fully united.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has taught the method of meditation. Now listen for the single word that crowns the entire path.

body.text: Among all yogis, the one who worships me with trust, with the inner self absorbed in me, is considered the most fully united. The word to hear is shraddhavan, trustful. It is not the skill of the posture but the trust of the heart that makes the worshipper the highest of all yogis. Krishna now explains how this trust is born, by revealing his divine knowledge to Arjuna.
